newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude business pressured by slim arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude business pressured by slim arb.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude business was limited Friday, impacted by the expiry of the October NYMEX crude contract.
U.S. traders said the market was centered on the lack of arbitrage possibilities for Brent.
All five of the Brent dates released from chains Friday were kept by British Petroleum, but the move was not enough to ease bearish feelings from overseas.
Market sources noted that BP kept the cargoes to profit from operational tolerance in its system.
Negative sentiment in the foreign crude markets was based on fundamental oversupply and the lack of arbitrage outlets, notably to the key U.S. market, crude brokers said.
Dated Brent mirrored the negative turn, confirmed done Friday at 48 cts below October paper, translating to a minus 5 cts to flat reading against Nov Brent, down 10-15 cts.
The closure of the arbitrage window was based largely on strong European refining margins, traders said.
In paper Brent business, the U.S. aftermarket saw a number of spread deals at slightly weaker levels.
Traders said the Oct/Nov spread was sold twice at +41 cts, and once at +42 cts, compared with a trio of deals earlier Friday at +44 cts.
Also seen in the U.S. window was a spread for Nov/Dec at +45 cts, roughly steady with deals seen earlier.

A total of 650 lots were traded for Nov Brent in the Friday window, all sold by a U.K. major between $21.93-$21.98, with 350 done at the $21.98 mark, and three separate 100 lot deals at $21.96, $21.95 and $21.95 respectively.
IPE Brent settled 8 cts lower at $21.98 a barrel.
In other business, a trade was seen in Nov Brent/Dubai at plus $2.05, well within established ranges.
Dec Brent/Dubai was talked around the same levels, while inter-month Dubai spreads were valued at 40 cts for Nov/Dec.
